cards.text: In this song, David, who would later become king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), talks straight to God. The note at the top says it's for the choirmaster, with stringed instruments, from when the Ziphites, people from the town of Ziph in Judah (Joshua 15:55), went to Saul, king of Israel (1 Samuel 15:1), and said, “Is David not hiding among us?” I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer and NOBODY came looking for me, but David can't even hide without the neighbors handing out DIRECTIONS!

cards.question: David's hiding, and the Ziphites are tipping off Saul. What's the first thing David asks God for in this song?

answers.text: To save him by His name
To hide him from Saul's army

cards.text: And David keeps asking: “Hear my prayer, O God; listen to the words of my mouth.” That's not a polite little “whenever you get a minute,” friend, that's ASAP.

cards.question: David begs God to hear his prayer and listen to the words of his mouth. Why is he pleading like this?

answers.text: Ruthless men are out to take his life
His own family has turned against him
He has fallen sick and can't get up

cards.text: David says these men have no regard for God. Then comes the word Selah, and the song keeps going.

cards.question: After the Selah, David says God has left him to face these ruthless men alone.

cards.text: Ruthless men are after his life, and David says, “Surely God is my helper; the Lord is the sustainer of my soul.” That's like the power going out and somebody calmly saying, “Relax, I know who's got the flashlight.”
Now David has something to say about his enemies.

cards.question: David says he'll pay his enemies back himself.

cards.text: David says of God, “He will reward my enemies with evil.” Then he prays, “In Your faithfulness, destroy them.”
Then David stops talking about his enemies and makes God a promise. I'll be honest, friend, my promises sound like “I'll wipe the flour off this counter TOMORROW.”

cards.question: David turns from his enemies to the LORD. What does he promise to do for Him?

answers.text: Build Him a house of cedar

cards.question: David also says he will praise the LORD's name because it is good.
David closes his song by giving the reason for his praise. What does he say God has done for him?

answers.text: Made him king over all Israel
Given him a city of his own

cards.question: After God delivers him, David says he still looks at his foes in fear.
